Chai, Not Cricket
Rajgarh, Uttar Pradesh. 5:12 AM.
The first bus to Meerut honks like it has been personally insulted.
{first}! Glasses. Now. The Meerut bus will be here in four minutes.
Four minutes. Pandey-ji's nets start in twenty. I can do both. Probably.
And don't think I didn't see the kit bag hiding behind the milk cans.
"It's nothing, Papa. Just for the evening."
Lie to keep the peace.
"Club trials today. Pandey-ji is picking boys."
Tell him the truth.
Club trials. The Sharma boy played club cricket too. You know what got him a job? The sugar mill.
Evening. Hm. Evening is when you help me close the stall. Remember that.
He knows. He always knows.
Bhaiya!! Papa, let him go. He's actually good. Bunty said he hit a six onto the masjid roof!
Bunty also says he saw a ghost near the water tank.
...That one is also true.
Papa almost smiles. Almost.
Pinky's geometry box broke. Her exam is on Monday. It's ₹120, beta. We don't have ₹120 this week.
Give Pinky your secret savings for the box.
She'll never forget it.
"I'll figure something out, Pinky."
A promise.
"Cricket first. Sorry, Pinky."
Focus.
Okay...
You press a folded note into her hand. Three months of saved bus fare.
Bhaiya. When you play for India, I'm going to tell everyone you bought me a compass.
Company Bagh Maidan. Three goats, one half-built wedding tent, and thirty boys pretending they're not nervous.
You. Gully bat. You're late.
I'm four minutes early.
In my nets, early is late. Pads on.
Pandey-ji's Nets
Three balls from the club's quickest net bowler. Pandey-ji is watching how your bat comes down. Survive.
Three balls. Three clean answers. A couple of the older boys stop talking.
The third one sneaks between bat and pad. The stump cartwheels. Somebody whistles.
Pandey-ji says nothing for a long time. Then he spits paan into the dust.
Your bat comes down from gully. Fix it, or go back to selling chai.
"Teach me. Whatever it takes."
He will make you suffer.
"My swing gets me runs, sir."
Back yourself.
Tomorrow. 5 AM. Bring a tyre.
A tyre? For what?
Runs in gully are free, beta. Wait until a real fast bowler aims at your nose.
A white SUV crunches onto the maidan. The boys go quiet. Even the goats look up.
Arre, chaiwala! Pandey-ji, you're letting tea boys into the nets now?
Vikrant Chauhan. Father: district association secretary. Bat: ₹45,000 English willow. He picks up yours.
Tape. More tape. Is this a bat or a mummy?
Laugh it off.
Swallow it. Stay calm.
"Nets. Six balls. You bowl, I bat."
Call him out.
Shove him into the sight-screen.
Feels great. Costs more.
Laughing? Good. Laugh tomorrow too. Six balls, chaiwala. Survive them and I'll stop calling you that.
It's over in ten seconds. Vikrant is on his back. Thirty boys are filming.
You're DEAD. My father will hear about this before dinner.
Six balls. Tomorrow. In front of everyone. Then you never come back here.
Ha! Fine. Tomorrow. Six balls. If you're still standing, I'll carry your kit bag. If not — you never come back.
At the scorer's table, a girl with a red pen has been watching all of it.
For the record, he bowls short when he's angry. I've scored his last nine matches.
Who is she?
Neha. Club scorer. Future sports journalist. Present... extremely bored.
Walk her home. It's getting dark.
A moment together.
"Thanks. Why are you helping me?"
Curious.
"I don't need help."
Proud.
Because Vikrant has never once said thank you to the scorer. See you tomorrow, chaiwala.
The streetlights flicker on one by one. Neither of you is in a hurry.
Everyone in this town has a plan for me. Marriage by twenty-two. B.Ed. Government job.
I want to be the one asking the questions at a press conference. Not making the tea for it.
Promise me something. If you ever make it — your first interview is mine.
"Deal. First interview. Front page."
"Only if you write that I'm handsome."
Front page is earned, cricketer. Not promised.
That night. Papa's phone buzzes on the shelf. He reads it twice. His face goes grey.
Satish ji namaste 🙏
₹30,000 by Sunday.
Or I come to the stall. With my people.
Papa sees you watching. He turns the phone face down.
Tomorrow: six balls against Vikrant. And Sunday is coming.
